ws.schild:jave-nativebin-osxm1 4.1.0 发布, The JAVE (Java Audio Video Encoder) library is Java wrapper on the 
        ffmpeg project. Developers can take take advantage of JAVE2 to transcode 
        audio and video files from a format to another. In example you can transcode 
        an AVI file to a MPEG one, you can change a DivX video stream into a 
        (youtube like) Flash FLV one, you can convert a WAV audio file to a MP3 or 
        a Ogg Vorbis one, you can separate and transcode audio and video tracks, 
        you can resize videos, changing their sizes and proportions and so on. 
        Many other formats, containers and operations are supported by JAVE2.

ws.schild:jave-nativebin-osx64 4.1.0 发布, DEPRECATED. This package carries the ffmpeg binary for intel macs.
        Apple ends support for intel hardware with macOS 27, so this package will be
        removed in a later release. On apple silicon use jave-nativebin-osxm1, which
        is unaffected. It is still built and published for now, and jave-all-deps
        still contains it, so nothing breaks today.

        The JAVE (Java Audio Video Encoder) library is Java wrapper on the

        artifacts you want without a version.

se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-cli 1.2.3 发布, Companion command-line tool for VibeTags: `init` bootstraps a project's opt-in
        files (file presence is the opt-in signal the processor honours), `doctor`
        reports the project's VibeTags health — build-tool wiring, active platforms,
        marker integrity. Run it without installing anything:

            jbang se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-cli:1.2.3 init --list

        The platform list and marker rules are read from vibetags-processor, so this
        tool cannot drift from what the processor actually does.

se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom 1.2.3 发布, Bill of Materials for the VibeTags annotation processor. Import this BOM to get
        a coherent vibetags-annotations + vibetags-processor pair without specifying
        each version individually.

        Recommended setup — annotations on the compile classpath, processor on the
        annotation-processor path only (the processor jar pulls in slf4j/logback,
        which has no business on consumer code's compileClasspath):

        Maven:
            <dependencyManagement>
                <dependencies>
                    <dependency>
                        <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
                        <artifactId>vibetags-bom</artifactId>
                        <version>1.2.3</version>
                        <type>pom</type>
                        <scope>import</scope>
                    </dependency>
                </dependencies>
            </dependencyManagement>

        Gradle:
            implementation platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.2.3')
            annotationProcessor platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.2.3')
            compileOnly 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations'
            annotationProcessor 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-processor'

        @AIIgnore, @AIPrivacy, @AICore, @AIPerformance). Zero third-party dependencies.
        All annotations use RetentionPolicy.SOURCE so they leave no trace in the
        consumer's compiled bytecode — this jar exists purely to give javac the
        symbols it needs at compile time.

        Pair this with vibetags-processor on the annotation-processor classpath:

            <dependency>
                <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
                <artifactId>vibetags-annotations</artifactId>
                <version>1.2.3</version>
